channel.title: Deepvac Engineering Blog
channel.description: Technical articles on thermal vacuum systems, space simulation, qualification testing, and TVAC engineering practice.

item.title: Used TVAC Chamber vs New: Evaluating the Second-Hand Market
item.description: A used vacuum chamber can cost a fraction of a new system – or the same, once controls, contamination history and adaptation are priced in. What to check before you buy.

item.title: Cryo Shrouds and Thermal Plates: How TVAC Chambers Get Cold
item.description: Radiative cold sink or conductive interface? How cryo shrouds and thermal plates are built, cooled and controlled – and when your test actually needs which.

item.title: Viewports and Optical Access in TVAC Chambers
item.description: From simple sight glasses to ZnSe windows for thermography and in-chamber IR cameras: how to plan optical access into a TVAC chamber – materials, ports and pitfalls.

item.title: Contamination Control in Thermal Vacuum Testing
item.description: Molecular films and particles can quietly degrade optics, sensors and coatings during a TVAC test. How contamination arises, how QCM and RGA measure it, and how you keep a campaign clean.

item.title: What Is Thermal Vacuum (TVAC) Testing?
item.description: An engineer's introduction to thermal vacuum testing: which space conditions a TVAC chamber simulates, why hardware fails in vacuum, and where the test sits in qualification.

item.title: Vacuum Levels Explained: From Rough Vacuum to UHV
item.description: The conventional vacuum ranges, how gas behaviour and equipment change with pressure, and why many thermal-vacuum specifications use the high-vacuum range.

item.title: TVAC Pumping Systems: How to Select the Right Architecture
item.description: From oil-free backing pumps to turbomolecular pumps, roots boosters and cryo traps: how a TVAC pumping system is structured, sized and monitored – and which drivers actually matter.

item.title: Testing Optics and Electronics in Vacuum: The Two Traps That Catch Bench-Proven Hardware
item.description: Electronics that run cool on the bench can overheat in vacuum, and clean-looking optics can grow molecular films. How to plan thermal vacuum tests for sensitive payloads.

item.title: In-House vs External TVAC Testing: A Decision Framework
item.description: Own chamber or test service? The answer depends on campaign cadence, iteration speed and hidden costs on both sides. A framework for the build-or-buy decision in environmental testing.

item.title: TVAC Automation: What a Modern Chamber Control System Does
item.description: Recipe execution, safety interlocks, data logging, alarming and remote access: why reproducible TVAC testing is above all a controls property.

item.title: ECSS, SMC-S-016 and NASA GEVS: Thermal Vacuum Test Standards Explained
item.description: How ECSS-E-ST-10-03C Rev.1, SMC-S-016 and NASA GEVS frame thermal-vacuum verification, how tailoring works and why project requirements remain binding.

item.title: TVAC Chamber Lead Time: What Actually Drives Delivery
item.description: The delivery time of a thermal vacuum chamber is set by engineering, long-lead components and acceptance testing – and partly by you. Where the time goes and how to shorten it.

item.title: TVAC Chamber Sizing: How to Choose the Right Volume
item.description: Nominal litres say little: how shroud, thermal plate and fixturing shrink usable volume, which clearances matter, cubic vs cylindrical geometry – and how much growth margin is sensible.

item.title: Solar Simulation vs Infrared Heating: Imposing Heat Flux in TVAC
item.description: Solar simulators, IR lamp arrays and heater plates all impose external heat flux in a thermal vacuum chamber – with very different fidelity, cost and complexity.

item.title: TVAC Facility Requirements: What Your Building Must Provide
item.description: Floor loads, transport path, power, heat rejection, LN₂ safety, cleanliness and IT: what a facility must provide before a thermal vacuum system arrives – with a practical site checklist.

item.title: Temperature Measurement in TVAC: Sensors, Mounting and Calibration
item.description: Thermocouple or PT100? How to select, mount and calibrate temperature sensors in vacuum – and deliver traceable data for qualification tests.

item.title: Electric Propulsion Testing in Vacuum: Why Thruster Facilities Are a Class of Their Own
item.description: A firing Hall or ion thruster turns the vacuum chamber into a continuous gas-load problem. What makes electric propulsion test facilities special – and how to scope one.

item.title: TVAC Test Types: From Thermal Cycling to Thermal Balance
item.description: Thermal vacuum cycling, thermal balance, bake-out, starts and soaks: what each TVAC test type verifies, how a typical profile looks and how qualification differs from acceptance.

item.title: Space Environment Simulation: Recreating Orbit on the Ground
item.description: Vacuum, a 3 K cold sink, 1361 W/m² of sunlight: what the thermal space environment does to hardware, how TVAC chambers replicate each element – and what no chamber can do.

item.title: Helium Leak Testing for TVAC Chambers: Methods, Units, Practice
item.description: How helium leak detection works, what leak rates in mbar·l/s actually mean, how virtual leaks differ from real ones – and when a chamber should be tested.

item.title: Outgassing in Vacuum: TML, CVCM and Bake-Out Explained
item.description: Why materials release gas in vacuum, how ECSS outgassing screening with TML and CVCM works, which materials cause trouble – and how bake-out, QCM and RGA keep contamination under control.

item.title: CubeSat TVAC Testing: What Small Satellites Really Need
item.description: Why thermal vacuum testing pays off even for CubeSats, what a typical campaign looks like, and how to right-size chamber and budget for 1U to 16U.

item.title: Inside a Thermal Vacuum Test Campaign: From Test Plan to Data Package
item.description: The traceable phases of a TVAC campaign, from requirements and setup through execution, anomaly handling and the final data package.

item.title: What Drives the Cost of a Thermal Vacuum Chamber?
item.description: The engineering choices that drive TVAC system cost: envelope, thermal concept, working pressure, interfaces, controls, documentation and lifecycle scope.

item.title: Key Requirements for Aerospace Qualification Testing
item.description: How programme-specific standards, thermal and vacuum boundaries, instrumentation and documentation shape TVAC qualification testing.

item.title: When Retrofit Makes More Sense Than Replacement
item.description: A condition-based framework for deciding whether to modernise an existing thermal-vacuum system or replace it.

item.title: Cooling Systems for Thermal Vacuum Chambers
item.description: How mechanical refrigeration, nitrogen-based cooling and combined concepts affect TVAC temperature range, infrastructure and operating effort.
